source.title: LLM Pretraining Shapes a Generalizable Manifold: Insights into Cross-Modal Transfer to Time Series
source.authors: Alexis Roger; Prateek Humane; Zheng-Han Tai; G. Legate; Andrei Mircea; Vasilii Feofanov; Irina Rish

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares the geometry of representations from differently initialized models using CKA and neighborhood visualizations, rather than testing convergence across model scale or using the original claim's broad cross-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper's own representation comparisons are the CKA and PCA/t-SNE analyses of LangInit and RandInit on synthetic waveforms. Its linear-probe, retrieval, crosscoder, and ablation results concern temporal structure or shared cross-domain features within one Qwen3 backbone; these do not test convergence across independent models as specified by the versions. Statements about the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and other prior work are citations, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study's own CKA and t-SNE comparison of two Qwen3-0.6B models bears on V3. The models share an architecture but start from different initializations: language-pretrained (LangInit) and random (RandInit). Both were then trained on time series. This is a new setting for V3, with different starting points rather than random seeds, measured by CKA rather than the original unit-matching method. The other analyses (probe, retrieval, crosscoder, ablation) stay inside one backbone.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that language pretraining builds a reusable sequential manifold and that finetuning is low-rank alignment onto it. They say the transfer mechanism is geometric rather than semantic. For the convergence comparison, they say LangInit and RandInit reach highly aligned relational geometry (CKA 0.855–0.988), arriving at functionally equivalent representations by different geometric paths. LangInit keeps a richer, more heterogeneous structure, while RandInit learns a simpler low-dimensional one.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CKA and qualitative PCA/t-SNE comparisons for a single pretrained-versus-random-initialized architecture on synthetic waveforms; it has no scale sweep or cross-architecture, paired cross-modal model comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The apparent geometry differs by visualization: PCA shows different global trajectories, while t-SNE shows similar local neighborhood structure. The authors also report that PCA trajectory complexity varies with input type.

fits_no_version.finding: Frozen pretrained hidden states can be linearly projected to realistic time-series trajectories without paired supervision. Random weights or random-token inputs largely fail to do so.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-pretrained representations contain decodable time-series structure before finetuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Retrieval among projected WikiText trajectories beats last-value carry-forward on MSE (1.91 vs 2.27).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projected LLM trajectories carry continuation signal for time series.

fits_no_version.finding: Crosscoder features fire on both time-series motifs and thematically linked text, within one backbone.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-domain temporal motifs share features within one model.

fits_no_version.finding: A Layer 1 head–MLP pair is superadditive for periodic time-series loss. Ablating the top-5 circuit raises WikiText loss by 4.53 nats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The same components serve periodic prediction and repetitive language modeling within one model.

record.problems: Only one backbone, one time-series corpus, and one tokenization scheme are used; the authors state that the geometric account is not verified at larger scale or on alternative architectures. The convergence comparison is a single LangInit–RandInit pair rather than a multi-seed study. The PCA/t-SNE comparison is qualitative, and uncertainty estimates for the reported CKA range and feature rates are not stated. The authors also note that their crosscoder analysis is incomplete and their causal-circuit evidence is preliminary.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported results bearing directly on the tested convergence versions were omitted. Forecasting training curves, effective-rank dynamics, and individual circuit-component sweeps were not entered as convergence rows because they do not directly compare cross-model alignment or shared subspaces.

untested.parts: There is no scale or capability sweep and no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
There are no vision–language or image–caption comparisons.
There are no multiple random seeds within one initialization regime, no comparison at the level of units or bases, and no layers other than 13 for CKA.
No model-to-model mapping or stitching is done. The linear probe maps one model's states onto time-series data.
The crosscoder features are shared between pretrained and finetuned states of one backbone, not across independent models.
No alternative similarity measures, settings or out-of-distribution inputs are used for cross-model alignment. The PCA/t-SNE plots are per-model visualizations.
There is no test of a plateau or of shared data or objectives as the explanation.

missing.what: Sine-wave PCA variance across layers is 72–73% for RandInit vs 25–41% for LangInit (17–49% vs 67–79% over all 28 layers). This describes representational form, not a cross-model similarity, so it would at most be context for V3.
missing.locator: Section 5.3, Figure 8 left; Appendix C, Figures 13–14

record.verdict_notes: The PRH and Convergent Learning papers are cited only as motivation. The V3 evidence is thin: one pair of models, one layer, five synthetic inputs, one seed, and no CKA baseline. There is also a tension the reader should note: CKA is invariant to rotation and scaling, yet the authors title Section 5.3 'FT and RI Find Different Solutions'. The record's V6 label was removed because PCA and t-SNE here are per-model visualizations, not alternative cross-model similarity measures. The tranche was changed from T2 to T3 because this is a new setting (pretrained vs random initialization, time-series domain).

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, nor comparison across different architectures, objectives, or training data.
No paired image-caption inputs or vision-language model comparison.

The comparison is a single pretrained-versus-randomly-initialized Qwen3-0.6B pair, not multiple independent training seeds within the same initialization regime; it does not compare individual units or identify a shared feature basis.
The linear probe maps frozen language-model states to time-series trajectories, not one model's representations onto another model's representations.
Crosscoder features are compared across pretrained and finetuned states/domains of one Qwen3 backbone, not across different models.
No systematic sweep of similarity settings such as neighbour count, and no out-of-distribution comparison of model-to-model alignment.
No test of a scale-dependent plateau, incomplete convergence across independent models, or whether shared training data/objectives rather than a common model of reality explain alignment.

rows.subject: LangInit vs RandInit (Qwen3-0.6B)
rows.stage_stated: both trained on time series; LangInit starts from pretrained weights and RandInit from random initialization
rows.operation_detail: CKA comparison of layer-13 representations for synthetic inputs
rows.note: The authors describe the representations as recovering nearly the same relational geometry up to rotation and scaling. The text reports a range across synthetic inputs, not per-input CKA values.
rows.check: CKA is reported only as a range across five synthetic inputs at layer 13, from a single training run (seed 420). There are no per-input values, no baseline (e.g. CKA against an untrained model), and no uncertainty.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.3; Appendix C describes the five synthetic inputs.

rows.subject: LangInit vs RandInit (Qwen3-0.6B)
rows.operation_detail: PCA visualization of layer-13 hidden-state trajectories

conditions.value: synthetic inputs; figure compares five waveforms

rows.measure: qualitative comparison of representation trajectories; variance captured by two PCs
rows.value: RandInit produces clean low-dimensional trajectories (62–92% PCA variance); LangInit produces more complex structured trajectories (34–98%), varying by input type.
rows.note: The paper says the two models encode temporal structure differently; the PCA plots are not a direct numerical distance between their representations.
rows.check: PCA is fit separately for each model–input pair (Appendix C), so the plots compare within-model variance, not cross-model alignment. They cannot show whether the two models share features or subspaces. They also do not test V6, because no alternative similarity measure is applied. The V6 link should be dropped.

rows.subject: LangInit vs RandInit (Qwen3-0.6B)
rows.operation_detail: t-SNE visualization of layer-13 hidden-state trajectories
rows.baseline: PCA visualization of the same setup
rows.value: The authors report similar local neighborhood structure in LangInit and RandInit; periodic inputs form smooth, phase-ordered curves in both.
rows.note: The authors contrast this local similarity with the different global geometries shown by PCA.
rows.check: This is a qualitative t-SNE (perplexity 30) observation of similar local structure. It is the same kind of evidence as r1 at layer 13 and is not a separate similarity metric. The V6 link that the record's label implies should be dropped.
